correctness.rationale: Every K_{a,b} count-state Markov transition is derived from independent fair ties and unanimous neighborhood majority; corners are exactly three closed classes. First-step equations for the two single-tie and double-tie states yield the rational exact time. Exact Bellman verification checks 1680 noncorner count states for all 1<=a,b<=8. The global 79/27 bound uses exhaustive exact-rational evaluation of 400 even-by-even size pairs 2..40 AND an analytic tail: p_42<1/8, monotone central binomial probabilities, and the ordered supersolution (11/5,13/5,41/15) bounding all cases with any even part >=42. Odd part sizes have no ties and expected times <=2. Unique equality at double-tied K_{2,6} and K_{6,2}. Finite tests alone are not treated as proof of unbounded n.

value.rationale: The prior work asks which network structures avoid long stochastic-majority stabilization. Complete bipartite two-community networks are canonical and graph sizes are unbounded; a fully explicit expected-time law with a uniform SHARP constant and a surprising finite-size nonmonotone extremizer K_{2,6} is a structural classification and benchmark, not a generic algorithmic observation. The analytic tail establishes a global maximum, and the exact formula informs every initial state. No general arbitrary-graph or pathwise bound is claimed.
